QUOTE: #ifndef MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member #else #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member #endif ... "the field is named `private_foo` for anyone who doesn't opt out" and "`library/common.h`... the library sees real member names everywhere... external users don't get it by including the public headers."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that opt-in code sees plain member names while ordinary public-header consumers see the `private_`-renamed ones.
